findings.current: —Monster Wave detected 3.2 kilometers to the east!
findings.defect: Reports the wave only to the east; the source says east and west.
findings.rationale: 동서쪽 names both directions, not east alone.
findings.replacement: —Monster Wave detected 3.2 kilometers away to the east and west!

findings.current: The rift had passed its threshold. The Collapse had begun.
findings.defect: Changes progression beyond the rift stage into a rift crossing its own threshold.
findings.rationale: 균열의 단계를 넘어 describes moving beyond the rift stage.
findings.replacement: The rift stage was over. The Collapse had begun.

findings.current: Thankfully, that laugh hadn’t been an ordinary person pretending to be a vicious criminal.
findings.defect: Reverses who would be pretending: the young man is reassured that the frightening-looking leader is not a criminal posing as an ordinary person.
findings.rationale: 흉악범의 일반인 코스프레 means a vicious criminal masquerading as an ordinary person.
findings.replacement: Thankfully, that laugh hadn’t come from a vicious criminal pretending to be an ordinary person.
findings.source: 다행히도 앞서 느낀 그 웃음은 흉악범의 일반인 코스프레가 아니었다.

findings.current: So far beneath the bottom that adding UCK to the end of his rank wouldn’t seem out of place.
findings.defect: Adding UCK to “F-rank” does not produce the source’s F-U-C-K joke.
findings.rationale: The suffix attaches to the letter F, spelling the insult.
findings.replacement: So far beneath the bottom that you could tack UCK onto the F and it would fit perfectly.
findings.source: 등급 뒤에 UCK를 붙여도 전혀 이질감이 없다는 밑바닥 아래의 지하.

findings.current: “Jesus, there he goes with the ‘back in my day’ again. The man lives on Mocha Gold.”
findings.defect: Loses the latte wordplay that prompts the exchange about Mocha Gold and White Gold.
findings.rationale: 그놈의 라떼 plays on the sound of the stock ‘back in my day’ phrase; the next lines continue the coffee joke.
findings.replacement:
“Jesus, here comes his ‘back in my day’ latte again.[^1] And all he ever drinks is Mocha Gold.”

[^1]: The Korean phrase for “back in my day” sounds like “latte,” setting up the instant-coffee joke.
findings.source: 염병, 그놈의 라떼 또 나왔네. 허구헌날 모카 골드만 처먹는 양반이.

findings.current: “Yeah. Almost every day for half a year. From the crack of dawn until evening, without missing a single day.”
findings.defect: Makes attendance ‘almost every day,’ contradicting the explicit statement that he missed no days. The approximation applies to the duration.
findings.rationale: 거의 modifies 반년, while 단 하루도 안 빼놓고 rules out missed days.
findings.replacement: “Yeah. For nearly half a year. From the crack of dawn until evening, without missing a single day.”
findings.source: 그래, 거의 반년 내내 그랬지. 단 하루도 안 빼놓고, 꼭두새벽부터 저녁까지.

findings.current: I remember the headline: *From F-rank to B-rank: The most dramatic rise of any Hunter.*
findings.defect: Turns the headline’s steep twists and turns in a Hunter’s life into an unqualified rise.
findings.rationale: 인생 굴곡 refers to life’s ups and downs, not solely upward advancement.
findings.replacement: I remember the headline: *From F-rank to B-rank: A Hunter’s Life of Extraordinary Ups and Downs.*
findings.source: F급에서 B급까지. 누구보다 가팔랐던 어느 헌터의 인생 굴곡.

summary: Actionable errors in the reported direction, a reversed comparison, the Collapse’s progression, and two jokes.
